A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL-MILP Solver research. All 16 pages of v3 and 17 pages of v4, including Appendices A–E, support comparison. The additional page accommodates an expanded Appendix B.

before.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1–3 report original experiments on generated MILP instances, including solver comparisons, neighborhood-size experiments, and architecture ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The two-phase rewards, actor-critic training, MPNN/Transformer architecture, and solution search remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. Appendix B expands the explanation of an existing reward.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same generated integer-only MILP datasets: D9×18, D50×20, D100×50, and D300×100. No dataset, task, domain, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Gurobi, local search, M_MLP, and M_CNN; Table 2 retains its local-search comparator. The architecture variants in Table 3 also match. The citation additions introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both report 100 test instances per dataset, 100-second main evaluations, 300-second neighborhood experiments, and a 600-second Gurobi run contributing to the best-known reference values. Metrics, preprocessing, model configurations, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: The beta sensitivity comparisons, neighborhood-size study, and component ablations are unchanged. The new Appendix B.1 figure illustrates the existing feasibility reward and supplies no additional experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain single-value result reporting without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–3 and their reported findings match. For example, Table 1 retains 100% feasibility and a 0.38% gap for RL-MILP on D100×50 with beta = 0.6. Appendix B adds no empirical outcomes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, reward equations, Proposition 1, and Appendix A assumptions and proof are unchanged. The added feasibility illustration introduces no new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about complete integer-variable solutions, incremental improvement, the proposed architecture, and optimal or near-optimal results. Minor wording edits do not alter contribution scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the bias parameter, attention mechanism, and neighborhood size remain unchanged, as does Section 4.3's qualification about lacking optimality guarantees. Appendix B.1 reillustrates the feasibility-reward rationale already explained in Section 3.1.3.

D1.justification: Appendices C–E retain the same pseudocode, data-generation parameters, hardware and software, optimizer settings, training-update counts, and implementation links. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v4 replaces Gasse et al. (2019) with Ding et al. (2020) in passages about primal heuristics and bipartite representations, and adds Zong et al. (2022) to the actor-critic discussion. These are limited citation changes; the overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Appendix B gains a feasibility-reward paragraph and is organized into B.1–B.3, separating feasibility, phase-2 optimization, and toward-optimal bias. Main-text changes are limited wording edits and updated cross-references; the overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 6, a schematic of feasibility improvement and deterioration. v3 Figures 6–7 are retained as v4 Figures 7–8, with the bias plots relocated to the additional appendix page. Main-text figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the reward design easier to follow by adding a feasibility illustration and separating Appendix B into clearly labeled explanations. This is a limited improvement in accessibility; the method, theoretical support, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
